correctness.rationale: Direct expansion yields two chirp-line orthogonality terms and mixed Gauss sums with relative sign η=χ(-1). Their phase difference is exactly −(b−2ca)(b−2da)/(2(c−d)); the invertible affine linear map (a,b)↦(u,v) gives q−1 off-line pairs for each nonzero field value. Surjective field trace gives q/p−1 nonzero trace-zero values, proving the nullity, every modulus multiplicity, and all parameters. Weyl conjugation diagonalizes the full lifted map with singular values √q|A|. Cauchy–Schwarz, Gauss modulus and minimum root-of-unity distances prove endpoints. Independently enumerated full complex sums on 11 finite fields and multiple slope pairs, including p-adic-degree 3, pass all comparisons and Parseval energy. No finite experiment was substituted for the all-field proof.

value.rationale: Coherent superposition of quadratic chirps is a canonical finite time-frequency window design family. The exact extension-field rank transition, kernel character label, full singular spectrum and sharp conditioning distinguish a positive informational-completeness result from systematic failures despite each chirp separately being a classical perfect sequence. These are natural operator invariants governing matrix tomography and stability, and the prime/extension trace obstruction is nontrivial rather than a parameter substitution. No general optimality is claimed.
